title: Not Just Yet. Egypt 2011: News - Incidents - Causes
author: Hussein Abdel-Razeq
target_audience: Readers interested in Middle Eastern politics
Students and scholars of modern Egyptian history
General readers seeking to understand the Arab Spring
Egyptian citizens reflecting on recent events
core_themes: Origins and triggers of the 2011 Egyptian revolution
Chronicle of political and social incidents in 2011
Analysis of the causes behind uprisings and mass protests
Impact of media and communication technologies
Civil society, youth movements, and calls for reform
primary_purpose: To document, synthesize, and analyze the events of the 2011 Egyptian revolution, offering readers a fact-driven account of the news, incidents, and underlying causes that led to the uprising, and providing social and political context for the changes witnessed.

structure_format.narrative_style: Analytical and reportorial, occasionally interspersed with editorial commentary
structure_format.organization: Sequential account of events by date, followed by thematic analysis of causes and outcomes
features: Summaries of news reports and official statements
Analytical reflections on roots and consequences

key_concepts_lessons: Large-scale social change is often rooted in the build-up of systemic grievances.
Media—especially social media—played a pivotal role in mobilizing the public and disseminating information.
Youths and civil society organizations were major drivers of the revolution, demonstrating the power of grassroots organization.
Political change comes with uncertainty and the need for sustained civic engagement post-uprising.
Understanding causes requires examining not just immediate triggers, but also long-standing issues such as police violence, unemployment, and corruption.
notable_features: Real-time capture of key moments of the Egyptian revolution
Examination of both the sequence of incidents and deep-rooted causes
Integration of news reports and on-the-ground testimonies
Contextual explanations accessible to non-expert readers
cultural_historical_context: Written amid and immediately following the 2011 Egyptian revolution, at a time when the Arab world was experiencing unprecedented calls for reform. The book serves as an early contemporary reflection on the social, political, and technological factors leading up to and shaping the events in Tahrir Square and beyond.
reception_impact: Regarded as an important eyewitness account and early analytical text on the Egyptian revolution
Valued for gathering and presenting contemporary sources during a period of rapid change
Referenced in regional political studies and by journalists covering the Arab Spring
Acknowledged by Egyptian readers as capturing the mood and complexities of the immediate post-Mubarak era
comparable_titles: The Square: The Story of a Revolution by Wael Ghonim
On Revolution Street: The Egyptian Revolution and Its Aftermath by Ashraf Khalil
Revolution 2.0: The Power of the People Is Greater Than the People in Power by Wael Ghonim
